title: Altermagnetism from a Cu-Fe Lieb Lattice in FeSe/Cuprate Heterostructures
authors: Ying Li, Augustin Davignon, Peng Rao, Runhan Li, Maia G. Vergniory, Roser Valentí, Johannes Knolle
abstract: Realizing altermagnetism in high-$T_c$ cuprate-based systems would provide a direct route for studying spin-split electronic bands in the absence of net magnetization and investigate their interplay with unconventional superconductivity. Here, we propose that FeSe/cuprate heterostructures offer such a platform, where a 45$^\circ$ twist of Cu and Fe layers creates an effective CuFe$_2$ Lieb lattice in which Fe magnetic order and Cu-Fe hybridization through the ligands induces altermagnetic $d$-wave spin splitting. A minimal tight-binding model shows that this mechanism is generic. Furthermore, a substrate-induced inequivalence of the two Se sites in FeSe provides a second route in which altermagnetism originates in the Fe layer and is transferred to the cuprate layer by proximity. Density functional theory calculations for FeSe/Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CuO$_6$ heterostructures confirm the viability of both mechanisms and reveal ways to enhance the spin splitting. These results establish superconducting cuprate/transition metal chalcogenide heterostructures as a promising setting for engineering altermagnetism and studying its coupling to unconventional superconductivity.
summary: This work proposes that FeSe/cuprate heterostructures are excellent platforms for studying altermagnetism—a state with spin splitting but no net magnetization. By modeling two distinct physical mechanisms (Lieb lattice coupling and substrate-induced symmetry breaking), the authors demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to host AM, which is crucial for understanding its interplay with unconventional superconductivity.
main_problem: The research aims to realize and study altermagnetism (AM) in high-temperature superconducting cuprate heterostructures to investigate spin-split electronic bands without net magnetization.
main_result: Both a Lieb lattice mechanism involving Cu-Fe hybridization and a proximity effect due to substrate-induced symmetry breaking are shown to be viable routes for engineering AM in FeSe/cuprate systems.
method: The study employs effective tight-binding models, parameterized using first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, to predict electronic band structures and spin conductivity.
model_or_system: The physical platform is the FeSe/cuprate heterostructure, modeled as an effective CuFe2 Lieb lattice. The Hamiltonian incorporates hopping terms ($t_0$ for Cu-Fe coupling and $\delta t$ for substrate-induced inequivalence in FeSe).
key_observables: Band splittings (d-wave splitting), spin conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}^z$), and orbital character of the electronic states.
important_parameters: $t_0$ (Cu-Fe hopping), $\delta t$ (substrate-induced hopping difference), and $U$ terms for correlation effects.
main_assumptions: The authors assume a checkerboard AFM ordering state for FeSe magnetism in some analyses, and they use DFT approximations (GGA+U) to derive model parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the heterostructure geometry, band splittings as functions of $t_0$ and $\delta t$, Fermi surfaces, and color plots showing enhanced spin conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}^z$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical motivation (AM in cuprates), then develops an effective tight-binding model incorporating two distinct AM mechanisms. DFT calculations are used to parameterize this model, leading to quantitative predictions of band splittings and spin transport properties.
why_interesting: While focused on strongly correlated magnetism, the use of proximity effects and engineered lattice structures mirrors concepts in quantum interface engineering relevant to AMO physics, particularly concerning tunable electronic couplings at boundaries.
